subject: Geo tethering & erase playbook request - FinHaven
messages:
From: Michael Stern <michael.stern@finhaven.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Hsu <elaine.hsu@finhaven.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo tethering and deletion playbook for LLM requests

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the product demo last week — the team at FinHaven liked the latency profile. Procurement and security asked me to kick off a focused Q&A so we can finish our vendor review. High-level asks below: 

1) Where are PII and inference payloads executed for the hosted Redwood API? We need a clear list of regions and cloud providers involved.
2) Which subprocessors touch inference payloads or transient caches (KV, prefix caches, logging/observability)?
3) Can you guarantee requests stay in the US only for our default use? If not, what isolation options do you offer (Dedicated/Private)?
4) Deletion SLA: for transient caches and for longer-term logs/metrics — what are timelines and contractual remedies?
5) Evidence: we need a short pack we can share with our legal/procurement (SOC 2 summary, subprocessor inventory, routing matrix).

I've attached our security questionnaire (FinHaven_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf). Can you confirm receipt and propose a time to review?

Appreciate a response early next week so we can move to the procurement queue.

Best,
Michael Stern
Director, Vendor Risk 
FinHaven
[Attachment: FinHaven_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Stern <michael.stern@finhaven.com>
Cc: Elaine Hsu <elaine.hsu@finhaven.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo tethering and deletion playbook for LLM requests

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear list. Confirm receipt of the questionnaire. We can absolutely put together a concise evidence packet and a short call to walk through specifics. High level answers below to unblock your team immediately: 

- Execution regions (hosted API): by default hosted inference runs on our multi-region US fleet (primary: us-east-1, us-west-2). For EU customers requests can be routed to eu-west-1 / eu-central-1; routing depends on customer region and model location.
- Subprocessors: primary compute/storage providers (AWS, GCP) for hosted; logging/observability uses a managed telemetry vendor (TraceHub) and S3-compatible object storage for transient artifacts. KV/prefix caches are kept in-memory on GPU nodes and ephemeral storage; we do not persist unencrypted inference payloads to long-term object storage.
- US-only: if you need strict US-only execution we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in US regions) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for full geographic isolation & contractual guarantees. Hosted can be configured with a US-only routing policy for most traffic, but the only way to get absolute assurance (including failover) is Dedicated/Private.
- Deletion SLAs: transient caches — typically cleared within 24 hours after request completion; ephemeral logs (debug/traces) — retained up to 30 days by default, can be reduced via config; aggregated billing/usage metrics — 90 days default (longer retention available as add-on). Contractual deletion commitments are included in our DPA and can be tightened for Dedicated/Private deployments.

I'll assemble the evidence packet (SOC 2 summary, subprocessor list, processing locations matrix) and loop Karthik (tech lead) and Marissa (solutions) to confirm any technical details. Are you available Tue 29 Jun 10:00–11:00 PT for a 30-min call?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-processing-locations-summary.pdf] [Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf]

- Evidence pack: we should include a simple one-pager mapping request path -> compute region -> subprocessor. I'll attach the latest subprocessor CSV and the US-only routing matrix.

I'll prepare the attachments and the one-page playbook (playbook should be human-friendly: bullet list + diagram link).

Karthik

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Stern <michael.stern@finhaven.com>
Cc: Elaine Hsu <elaine.hsu@finhaven.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo tethering and deletion playbook for LLM requests

Michael / Elaine — thanks for taking time today. Per our discussion, attaching the promised artifacts and summarizing the key commitments in plain language so your legal/procurement can review quickly.

Quick summary (what happens to an inference request):
- Inbound request lands on our API gateway in the requested region (by default US multi-region fleet: us-east-1 or us-west-2).
- Routing: policy-based. Hosted customers get region-prefers; if you choose US-only routing we prefer US sites. Note: in rare capacity constraints we have an automated fallback to the nearest compatible US region (not cross-border) for the US-only routing policy.
- Execution: model inference executes on GPU instances in the chosen region. KV/prefix caches are in-memory on those instances and are ephemeral.
- Logging/observability: request traces and debug logs are sent to our telemetry vendor (TraceHub) and retained per configured retention windows. PII is redacted by default in structured logs; raw inference payloads are not written to long-term object storage by default.

Deletion & contractual options we provide:
- Transient caches (KV/prefix): cleared automatically within 24 hours; for Dedicated/Private we can provide an API-triggered immediate purge and certificate of deletion.
- Traces/debug logs: default 30-day retention; can be reduced to 7 days or removed on request for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Billing/usage metrics: 90-day retention by default; archival options available.
- Contractual guarantees: our DPA (link below) includes deletion commitments; Dedicated/Private customers get stronger SLAs and the option for on-prem key management (HSM/KMS).

Subprocessors & evidence provided:
- Attached: subprocessor-inventory.csv — lists cloud compute providers (AWS, GCP), telemetry vendor (TraceHub), identity provider (Okta), and object storage partners.
- Attached: us-only-routing-matrix.csv — simple matrix showing how requests map to regions under the US-only routing policy.
- Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf — SOC 2 coverage summary and scope.

Next steps we recommend for procurement:
1) We can provide a tailored DPA with FH-specific routing & deletion windows.
2) If you need absolute physical isolation, we will propose Redwood Dedicated capacity in US zones (pricing & procurement steps in the HubSpot deal).
3) If you want an engineering workshop, Karthik can run a 60-min tech deep-dive and provide a signed evidence packet.

Links: DPA (https://docs.redwood.ai/DPA) | HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/789234)

Hope this helps — attaching the files for your review. If procurement wants to tighten retention windows in the contract we can map precise language.

Best regards,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
